state_code: # SOURCES (all fetched 2026-10-01 from ospi.k12.wa.us; no Internet Archive fallback needed)
# - Excel with Crosswalk tab (v3.1, "Final adoption version"): https://ospi.k12.wa.us/sites/default/files/2026-08/math26-final-adoption-spreadsheet.xlsx
# - Adoption statement in the standards doc: "Adopted on this 18th day of June 2026," signed by Superintendent Chris Reykdal.

# - Landing page: "Educators have the 26-27 school year to begin exploring, learning about, and using the newly revised standards. The standards are required to be used with students in the 27-28 school year."
# CODE FORMAT: M.<grade>.<domain>.<category>.<number>  e.g. M.3.R.MD.5 = Math, grade 3, Relationships, CCSS domain MD, CCSS standard number 5.
# - Category = the original CCSS domain abbreviation (CC, OA, NBT, NF, MD, G) plus new DS (data science). Number = the CCSS standard number, kept on purpose; CCSS cluster letter is dropped.
# - Lettered indicators (a, b, c...) appear in the text but are not separate codes; they mirror CCSS sub-parts and are folded into their standard here.
# - Every K-5 CCSS standard maps 1:1 to a WA code with the same grade, category and number (OSPI Crosswalk tab); only the domain letter(s) are new.
# DOMAINS: DA = Data Analysis; Q = Quantity (written "Quantities" in the Word doc's coding key, "Quantity" elsewhere); R = Relationships; SR = Spatial Reasoning.
# - Same CCSS domain can be split across WA domains, e.g. grade 3 MD sits in SR (MD.1, MD.8), DA (MD.2-4) and R (MD.5-7).
# ROW COUNTS (K-5): 172 = 148 CCSS-derived (135 same, 13 edited, 0 moved) + 24 new (DS.1-4 in each grade K-5).

# KIND RULE: "same" = identical or reworded without changing math scope (incl. "Fluently" -> "Efficiently, flexibly, and accurately", added "real world", dropped examples/footnotes). "edited" = scope actually changed (list below).
# CCSS K-5 DROPPED: none. All 148 K-5 CCSS codes appear in the Crosswalk tab.
# - New data science category DS (4 standards per grade, all in DA): pose questions, collect/consider data, analyze/visualize, interpret/communicate. OSPI lists them with CCSS "NA".
#   Partial overlap with CCSS data standards (left out of ccss column because OSPI marks them NA): M.1.DA.DS.3 ~ 1.MD.C.4; M.2.DA.DS.2 ~ 2.MD.D.10; M.3.DA.DS.3 ~ 3.MD.B.3.
# - Memorization of facts removed: 2.OA.B.2 (sums from memory), 3.OA.C.7 (products from memory).
# - Standard algorithm no longer required ("strategies or algorithms"): 4.NBT.B.4, 5.NBT.B.5; 3.NBT.A.2 drops "and algorithms".
# - Rounding reframed as estimation with varied strategies: 4.NBT.A.3, 5.NBT.A.4; "including rounding" dropped from 3.OA.D.8, 4.OA.A.3. (3.NBT.A.1 rounding to 10/100 is unchanged.)
# - 1.OA.C.6 now "add within 20, and subtract within 10" (CCSS: add and subtract within 20).
# - Line plots: fixed units (1/2, 1/4, 1/8) removed from 4.MD.B.4 and 5.MD.B.2.

# - Many standards gain "efficiently, flexibly, and accurately", "real world", visual models, or reasonableness checks (e.g. 5.NF.B.3, 5.NF.B.6, 5.MD.A.1); 5.NBT.B.6 names partial quotients. Treated as same.

# - same/edited is my judgement from comparing CCSS text (Crosswalk tab col C) to WA text (Word doc / K-8 tab). Borderline "same": 1.OA.B.3, 3.NF.A.1, 4.NF.A.1, 4.NF.B.3 stem, K.G.B.6 (now explicitly 2-D shapes).
# - The Crosswalk tab's WA text differs slightly from the Word doc / K-8 tab in ~25 rows (typos, an omitted example, word order); codes agree everywhere. Word doc treated as authoritative.
# - An earlier June 2026 Word file (.../2026-06/wa-learning-standards-mathematics_0.docx) exists; the Aug 2026 v3.1 files were used.
